chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Ibn Abī Ḥamzah, he said:
I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام: at how much is the thief's hand cut off? So he brought his two palms together, then said: “At their number in dirhams.”

So this does not contradict what we mentioned previously, that the minimum amount for which the thief is cut off is a quarter of a dinar, because it is not impossible that the value of the dirhams to which he pointed was a quarter of a dinar. And Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام clarified that in the narration of Muḥammad ibn Muslim which we mentioned at the beginning of the chapter, when he was asked about one who stole two dirhams, and he said: “At a quarter of a dinar, whatever value the dinar may have reached.”

key_terms.الدَّرَاهِمِ: silver dirhams used as a measure of monetary value
key_terms.السَّارِقُ: the thief, the person accused of theft
key_terms.حَدَّ: the prescribed legal punishment or limit in sacred law
key_terms.رُبُعُ دِينَارٍ: one quarter of a dinar, the legal threshold mentioned for theft
key_terms.يُقْطَعُ: has the hand cut off as the prescribed hadd punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of stolen property that warrants the hadd punishment for theft in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report addresses the legal threshold at which the hadd punishment for theft applies. It explains that the mention of a number of dirhams is reconciled with other narrations specifying a quarter of a dinar by understanding the dirham amount as equal in value to a quarter of a dinar.
